replies.Briefly, how do you perform a Principal: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a statistical technique used to reduce the dimensionality of a dataset while retaining as much variability as possible. The steps involve standardizing the data, computing the covariance matrix, calculating the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the covariance matrix, sorting the eigenvalues in descending order, and selecting the top k eigenvalues and their corresponding eigenvectors to form a feature vector. Finally, you transform the original dataset into the new subspace using the feature vector. While the mathematics behind PCA can be complex, you shouldn't get too anxious about it.
